post.headline: Put every intake role on the notice list
post.subtext: A recipient can name multiple contacts so newsroom duties do not depend on one person passing the word.
post.image_alt_text: Light-mode social graphic headed “Put every intake role on the notice list,” beside Hush Line’s Notifications settings with Tip Notifications on, three recipient email addresses marked Enabled with PGP key configured, and an Add Recipient button.

social.bluesky: Incoming reports may involve an editor, standards lead, and board member. Hush Line’s Notifications page can name several contacts. The Tip Notifications switch turns this on, Add Recipient expands the roster, and a PGP key can be configured per contact. Compare the roster with current duties.
social.linkedin:
Responsibility for incoming reports rarely sits with one role.

On Hush Line’s Notifications page, a recipient can name several contacts, such as an editor, standards lead, and board member. The Tip Notifications switch turns this on, while Add Recipient expands the roster. A PGP key can be configured for every contact.

This gives a newsroom a visible way to cover several duties without depending on one person to relay the news.

Open Notifications and compare the roster with today’s duty list.
social.mastodon:
When incoming reports are divided across roles, one person should not have to relay every arrival.

Hush Line’s Notifications page can name several contacts. The Tip Notifications switch turns this on, Add Recipient expands the roster, and a PGP key can be configured for every contact.

Check the roster against current newsroom duties.

post.rationale: The sole eligible screenshot is a cooldown fallback, so this plan takes a distinct role-coverage angle instead of repeating the recent post about notification-address privacy. It shows recipient teams how separate email addresses and PGP keys can help the staff responsible for intake learn that a tip arrived while review stays in the Hush Line inbox. The hook names a concrete newsroom workflow, and the CTA asks teams to compare the recipient list with actual staff responsibilities.
post.copy_brief: Write for recipients and staff using Hush Line day to day, not for platform admins.
